title: Sebastian and the Letters
premise: Marine biologist Ansel Blackwood fled to a remote Scottish island research station after a devastating breakup, finding safety in data and sea turtles. When a waterlogged letter postmarked eleven years ago washes up in a turtle nest survey, she discovers it was written by her — and never sent — to Sebastian Hale, the man who left her without goodbye. The letter's arrival coincides with Sebastian's return to the island as the new ferry engineer, forcing both to confront what actually happened the night they parted. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Ansel must choose between a prestigious post abroad and the love she finally understands was never lost, only misplaced — and she chooses Sebastian, staying to build a life where her past and present finally belong to each other.
about_author: Elodie Ravensworth is a former marine conservation volunteer who spent three summers on Scottish islands before turning to fiction full-time. She writes love stories about people who rebuild themselves in wild, salt-scoured places.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Opening on the island research station, Ansel counts turtle nests with methodical precision, established as a woman who has organized her entire life around avoiding feeling. Emotional beat: guarded contentment that is clearly a fortress.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. During a beach survey, volunteer Finn uncovers a plastic-protected letter wedged in the dunes. Ansel recognizes her own handwriting and freezes: it's the letter she wrote Sebastian the night he left, never sent. Emotional beat: shock and dread.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with flashback fragments. She reads the letter alone at night, remembering the boy she loved and the night everything ended. She hides it from her colleagues. Emotional beat: grief reopened, old wounds made new.

chapters.title: The Ferry Comes In
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian Hale steps off the seasonal ferry as its new engineer, returning to the island that broke him. He sees Ansel on the dock and his chest tightens. Emotional beat: dread laced with longing.

chapters.title: Salt in the Old Wound
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Forced proximity: Sebastian's ferry schedule intertwines with her supply runs. Their first conversation is brittle, professional, loaded. Emotional beat: hostility masking hurt.

chapters.title: Finn Asks Too Many Questions
chapters.summary: Finn's POV. The young volunteer senses the tension between Ansel and the ferryman and starts playing amateur matchmaker, while revealing how much Ansel has quietly become family to the station crew. Emotional beat: warmth, found family established.

chapters.title: The Night He Left, Retold
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, extended flashback. We learn Sebastian left because of a family crisis he never explained, believing he was protecting Ansel from his father's collapse and debts. Emotional beat: tragic misunderstanding crystallized.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A storm strands Sebastian at the station overnight. Trapped together, they circle the past without landing, and old intimacy flickers dangerously. Emotional beat: tension, almost-confession.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hatchlings emerge; the whole station turns out to guide them to the sea. Sebastian shows up uninvited and works beside her, and something softens. Emotional beat: tentative reconnection, hope.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A prestigious marine institute in Lisbon offers Ansel a permanent lead position — the career validation she's chased for a decade, starting the week after the last ferry. Emotional beat: ambition colliding with unease.

chapters.title: Coffee, Two Sugars
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian learns of the Lisbon offer from gossip at the harbor. He resolves to keep his distance, then fails spectacularly by bringing her coffee the way she used to take it. Emotional beat: tenderness he can't suppress.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Argument
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the old lighthouse, the past finally detonates: she accuses him of abandonment; he accuses her of never asking why. Neither tells the whole truth. Emotional beat: rupture, the relationship seemingly dead again.

chapters.title: What Ansel Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel decides to leave early, accepting Lisbon. She packs, drafts her resignation from the island, and rereads the eleven-year-old letter — realizing she wrote 'I would have followed you if you'd asked.' Emotional beat: bitter clarity.

chapters.title: Sebastian's Confession to the Sea
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian tells the harbor master — a father figure — the full story of his father's ruin and the shame that drove him away. The old man tells him shame kept him away, not love. Emotional beat: catharsis, resolve.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Finn's POV. Finn, cleaning the station archive, finds the letter's second page — the part Ansel never read, torn away by water — and delivers it. It contains Sebastian's address from eleven years ago: he waited for a reply that never came. Emotional beat: revelation, everything reframed.

chapters.title: He Waited
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian, unaware the letter surfaced, prepares to leave the island for good after the season's final run, writing his own unsent letter. Emotional beat: quiet heartbreak, symmetry with Ansel.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel boards the last ferry to the mainland with her Lisbon acceptance in her bag — and Sebastian at the helm. Mid-crossing she finally reads the recovered page and understands he waited. Emotional beat: rising panic and hope.

chapters.title: Midchannel
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In open water, storm clouds gathering, Ansel confronts Sebastian at the wheel. Truths spill: his father, her silence, eleven lost years. The ferry turns back — engine trouble or choice, neither cares. Emotional beat: climax, raw and cathartic.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finally Delivered
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back on the island dock in the rain, Ansel hands Sebastian the water-stained letter. He reads it while she watches. He answers it aloud, word for word, the reply he composed at nineteen. Emotional beat: the kiss, eleven years late.

chapters.title: Choosing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel calls Lisbon and declines — but negotiates a collaboration that keeps the island station funded and her career intact, refusing the false choice between love and work. Emotional beat: agency, maturity, relief.

chapters.title: The Station at Winter
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The off-season island: Finn staying on, the harbor master's blessing, Sebastian's ferry refitted for winter runs, Ansel's new research season planned. The found family gathers for a storm-bound dinner. Emotional beat: belonging, warmth.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Letters
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. One year later, the couple mails the two old letters — hers and his — to each other from the island postbox, a ritual of no longer unsending things. On the beach, a new nest of hatchlings makes for the sea. Emotional beat: peace, full-circle resolution.
